items.title: Minecraft Was Missing One Brilliant Idea
items.excerpt: Two Minute Papers breaks down Terrain Diffusion — a diffusion-model mod (shipping on Modrinth/GitHub) that generates far richer, more varied Minecraft terrain than the game's hand-tuned noise system. A concrete example of generative AI as a real procedural-content-generation tool a game's modders/designers can actually install and use.

items.title: PC ports of old console games are the new AI vibe coding battleground
items.excerpt: With projects like Donkey Kong 64 Recompiled, human programmers are staking a claim on the craft of retro recompilation as a wave of AI-vibe-coded ports floods in — a look at how LLM-assisted coding is reshaping (and contesting) the workflow of bringing old games to PC.

items.title: Meccha Chameleon awarded Steam's highest honor: a fast-follow AI ripoff that even uses the same name in some regions
items.excerpt: A generative-AI 'fast-follow' clone of the co-op hit Scribble Hunt tops a Steam chart — even reusing the original's name in some regions — spotlighting how cheap AI content pipelines are accelerating storefront clone-flooding. Borderline culture/slop item; flagged for the curator to weigh against the two workflow picks.
